title: All at sea: Meaning and Examples — Word Power 31
content:
## All at sea

**Word Power 31 · English idioms**

### Meaning

Confused or uncertain.

### Usage

1. I'm all at sea with these new instructions.
2. Most of the students are at sea in English.

### How to use it

All at sea describes confusion or uncertainty. With can introduce the subject causing the difficulty. The phrase is figurative: the speaker need not be on a boat or near water.

### Another example

I was all at sea with the new timetable until a classmate explained the changes.

### Check your understanding

Complete: Without the instructions, we were all at ___. (sea / water)

### Suggested answer

Sea. This fixed expression means confused. Changing the noun loses the idiomatic meaning.
